title: The Norton Anthology of English Literature, Vol. E: The Victorian Age (1830–1901), 11th edn
author_or_editor: Stephen Greenblatt (gen. ed.), Catherine Robson and Rachel Ablow (vol. eds.)
reliability_notes: Confirmed via Norton/Wiley adoption listings and Princeton library catalog. Victorian volume is E, not D (D = Romantic, 1785–1832).

title: The Oxford Dictionary of National Biography, 60 vols
author_or_editor: H. C. G. Matthew and Brian Harrison (eds.)
reliability_notes: 60-vol print set + index confirmed by OUP/LRB reporting; Harrison died Oct 2004 and Lawrence Goldman succeeded him as co-editor — cite the 2004 set as Matthew & Harrison.

title: The Poems of Tennyson, 2nd edn, 3 vols (Longman Annotated English Poets)
reliability_notes: NYPL/Hathi records: 1st edn 1969, the standard 3-vol set is the 2nd edn of 1987.

title: The Poems of Robert Browning (Longman Annotated English Poets)
author_or_editor: John Woolford, Daniel Karlin and Joseph Phelan (eds.)
reliability_notes: Browning Society/series records confirm the three-editor team and the 1991 start. check_first: the total number of volumes in the completed set (5 or 6).

title: The Works of Elizabeth Barrett Browning, 5 vols
reliability_notes: NYPL MARC record, ISBN 9781851969005, confirms 5 vols, Donaldson, 2010.

title: The Letters of Charles Dickens, Pilgrim Edition, 12 vols
author_or_editor: Madeline House, Graham Storey and Kathleen Tillotson (gen. eds.)
reliability_notes: Dickens Journals Online's bibliographic page states "12 vols (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1965–2002)" — my first guess of 14 vols/1973 was wrong. Serial texts of Household Words / All the Year Round are covered by Dickens Journals Online (Buckingham, 2009–; gen. ed. Paul Schlichr with Andrew MacGibbon), verified but held in RESERVE.

title: Vanity Fair: A Novel without a Personality (Riverside Edition)
reliability_notes: Catalog record for the Riverside Edition confirms both editors and 1963. The 17-vol "Oxford Thackeray" (ed. Saintsbury) was also checked but the OUP volume dates vary, so it is not used as a row.

title: The Clarendon Edition of the Novels of the Brontës
author_or_editor: Ian Jack (gen. ed.), with Herbert Rosengarten (textual ed.)
reliability_notes: Series start (Jane Eyre, 1969) and gen. ed. confirmed by OUP records. check_first: the individual volume editors and dates — the Jane Eyre volume's editor name is recorded inconsistently in catalogs. One row covers Charlotte and Emily Brontë.

title: The Collected Letters of George Gissing
author_or_editor: Paul F. Mattheisen, Arthur C. Young and Pierre Coustillas (eds.)
reliability_notes: Athens/Ohio UP records confirm the three editors and the 1990–1997 run. check_first: the number of volumes (catalogs differ, 6 vs 9, depending on the issue) — title, editors, publisher and dates are firm.

title: Esther Waters, first book edition
reliability_notes: Publication first appeared in the Speaker (1894); the first book edition is Walter Scott Publishing Co., March 1894. My first guess of William Heinemann was wrong — Heinemann is Moore's later publisher.

title: The Time Machine: An Invention, first edition in book form
reliability_notes: Book publication May 1895 (simultaneous US edition, Henry Holt, 1895); the story had been serialised in The Observer (December 1894 – February 1895) before the Heinemann volume. Imprint and year confirmed in bibliographic records.

title: The Symbolist Movement in Literature
reliability_notes: First edition confirmed in catalog/auction records. A modern scholarly reprint with Matthew Creasy's introduction is Fyfield Books / Manchester University Press, 2014 — either can be cited; the 1900 Heinemann text is used here.

title: Middlemarch: A Norton Critical Edition
reliability_notes: Norton record ISBN 9780393877199; text follows the 1874 revised (author's final) text. George Eliot's correspondence is covered by Gordon S. Haight, The George Eliot Letters (Yale UP, 1954–1978), verified but held in RESERVE.

title: The Letters of Mrs Gaskell
author_or_editor: J. A. V. Chapple and Arthur Pollard (eds.)
reliability_notes: Standard scholarly edition; reprinted with revisions 1997. Publisher and editors confirmed in library catalogs.

title: The Collected Letters of Thomas Hardy, 7 vols
author_or_editor: Richard Little Purdy and Michael Millgate (eds.), later volumes Michael Millgate and Keith Wilson
reliability_notes: Volume sequence and editors confirmed across OUP/catalog records; a supplement volume appeared in 2012. check_first: attribution of the 2012 supplement as vol. 8.

title: The Way We Live Now (Oxford World's Classics, 2nd edn)
reliability_notes: ISBN 9780198705031 confirms editor and edition. check_first: the exact reprint year of this OWC 2nd edn (2009 vs later impression).

title: Selected Works of Anthony Trollope, 62 vols in 36 titles (facsimile edition)
reliability_notes: Two independent sources (a Springer bibliography of Trollope editions and the encyclopedia.com Hall entry) state 62 vols, Arno Press, 1981. This is the real Trollope scholarly set — the "Ohio State Press Cornell series" in the task brief could not be traced (see UNRESOLVED).

title: The Rossetti Archive
publisher: University of Virginia / Institute for Advanced Technology in the Humanities
reliability_notes: IATH project record confirms director and 1993 start (core NEH funding 1993–2008). Covers D. G., William Michael and Christina Rossetti.

title: The Collected Works of William Morris, 24 vols
reliability_notes: University of Iowa Morris & Friends collection confirms 24 vols, May Morris, Longmans. My first guess of 23 vols was wrong.

title: Culture and Anarchy and Other Writings (Cambridge Texts in the History of Political Thought)
reliability_notes: CUP series page confirms Collini and 1993.

title: Poems and Ballads, first edition
reliability_notes: Rossetti Archive/bibliographic records and auction catalogues give Moxon as the 1866 publisher. check_first: one bookseller attributes the first edition to John Camden Hotten — Moxon (with the Moxon & Co. issue variant) is the better-supported statement.

title: The Poems of Gerard Manley Hopkins, 4th edn
author_or_editor: W. H. Gardner and N. H. MacKenzie (eds.)
reliability_notes: Confirmed as the standard scholarly text; the first edition was 1918, ed. Robert Bridges.

title: Apologia Pro Vita Sua
reliability_notes: Oxford English Texts series record confirms Svaglic and 1967.

title: The Renaissance: Studies in Art and Poetry — the 1893 Text
author_or_editor: Walter Pater, ed. Donald L. Hill
reliability_notes: UC Press catalog + library MARC confirm Hill's 1893-text edition, 1980. My first guess (an Oxford or Princeton edition of 1971) was wrong.

title: The Works of John Ruskin, Library Edition, 39 vols
author_or_editor: E. T. Cook and Alexander Wedderburn (eds.)
reliability_notes: Confirmed by the standard Ruskin bibliographies (Library Edition, limited to 2,062 copies).

title: The Collected Works of John Stuart Mill, vol. XVIII: Essays on Politics and Society I (incl. On Liberty)
author_or_editor: J. M. Robson (ed.), intro. Alexander Brady
reliability_notes: University of Toronto Press published-volume record confirms vol. XVIII, Robson as editor and 1977 (London: Routledge & Kegan Paul is the co-publisher — not used as the citation).

title: The Correspondence of Thomas Carlyle and Ralph Waldo Emerson, 1834–1872, 2 vols
publisher: Chatto & Windus (London); Boston: Ticknor and Co.
reliability_notes: Duke-Edinburgh/Carlyle bibliographies give 1883, Chatto & Windus (Norton was the editor). My first guess of Chapman & Hall, 1882 was wrong.

title: The Annotated Origin: A Facsimile of the First Edition of On the Origin of Species
publisher: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press
reliability_notes: Harvard UP record confirms Costa as annotator. My first guess (Janet Browne) was wrong — Browne is the author of a Darwin biography, a different book.

title: The First Principles
reliability_notes: First-edition imprint confirmed in bibliographic records; the same publisher issued The Study of Sociology in installments 1873 (US: Appleton).

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray (Oxford World's Classics)
reliability_notes: OUP record confirms Bristow's edition and 2008. The Complete Letters of Oscar Wilde (eds. Merlin Holland and Rupert Hart-Davis, Fourth Estate, 2000) is verified but trimmed — see RESERVE.

title: The Cambridge Companion to George Bernard Shaw
reliability_notes: CUP series record confirms Innes as editor of the 1998 Cambridge Companion volume.

title: Heart of Darkness: A Norton Critical Edition, 3rd edn
reliability_notes: Norton record confirms Kimbrough's edition; the NCE line ran 1963 (1st) – 1971 (2nd) – 1988 (3rd).

title: The Norton Anthology of American Literature, 9th edn
reliability_notes: Norton catalog + library records confirm Levine as gen. ed. of the 9th edn and 2017. check_first: the per-volume editor names for vols A–F; the whole-set citation is solid.

title: Leaves of Grass: A Textual Variorum of the Printed Poems, 3 vols (The Collected Writings of Walt Whitman)
author_or_editor: Sculley Bradley, Harold W. Blodgett, Arthur Golden and William White (eds.)
reliability_notes: Confirmed as the variorum of the printed editions of Leaves of Grass from 1855 through 1881–82, issued under the Collected Writings of Walt Whitman umbrella.

title: The Walt Whitman Archive
author_or_editor: Ed Folsom and Kenneth M. Price (gen. eds.), later Matt Cohen and others as project editors
publisher: Center for Digital Research in the Humanities, University of Nebraska–Lincoln
reliability_notes: Archive's own credits page confirms the general editors and host. check_first: the founding year (1995 vs 1996 first funding cycle).

title: The Poems of Emily Dickinson: Variorum Edition, 3 vols
publisher: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press
reliability_notes: HUP record (ISBN 9780674676220), Emily Dickinson Museum edition list and JSTOR review all confirm 3 vols, Belknap, 1998; the 1-vol Reading Edition followed in 1999. There is no "California edition" of Dickinson (see UNRESOLVED).

title: The Poems of Emily Dickinson, 3 vols
publisher: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press
reliability_notes: HUP feature page, the Dickinson archive's edition guide and a 1956 JSTOR review all confirm Belknap/1955/3 vols — the first complete scholarly text.

title: Moby-Dick; or, The Whale, vol. 6 of the Northwestern-Newberry Edition of the Writings of Herman Melville
author_or_editor: Harrison Hayford and Hershel Parker (eds.), with G. Thomas Tanselle (gen. ed. of the series)
publisher: Northwestern University Press (with the Newberry Library)
reliability_notes: NUP records and library catalogs confirm NNME vol. 6, Moby-Dick, 1988, Hayford & Parker as volume editors and Tanselle as general editor of the series. check_first: the exact order of names as printed on the volume title page.

title: The Centenary Edition of the Works of Nathaniel Hawthorne
author_or_editor: William Charvat, Roy Harvey Pearce and Claude M. Simpson (gen. eds.), with Fredson Bowers and L. Neal Smith (textual eds.)
reliability_notes: Series title page/OSU records: 23 vols, 1962–1997, publication place Columbus.

title: The Collected Works of Edgar Allan Poe, 3 vols (Tales; Poems; Essays and Reviews)
publisher: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press
reliability_notes: Harvard UP records confirm Mabbott as editor and the 1969–1978 publication span of the three volumes (Tales 1969; Poems and Essays and Reviews 1978, issued after Mabbott's death with editorial assistance).

title: The Collected Works of Ralph Waldo Emerson, vol. I: Nature, Addresses, and Lectures
author_or_editor: Robert E. Spiller and Alfred R. Ferguson (eds.)
publisher: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press
reliability_notes: Harvard's Emerson project volume list. check_first: the 1960 date sometimes cited for vol. I vs the 1969 Belknap printing.

title: The Writings of Henry D. Thoreau
reliability_notes: Princeton's Collected Writings pages confirm Witherell and the ongoing scholarly edition. My first guess of Yale University Press was wrong — Yale publishes only individual Thoreau titles, e.g. Walden: A Fully Annotated Edition, ed. Jeffrey S. Cramer (Yale UP, 2004, ISBN 0300104669), which is verified but held in RESERVE.

title: Woman in the Nineteenth Century: A Norton Critical Edition
author_or_editor: Margaret Fuller, ed. Larry J. Reynolds
reliability_notes: Norton record ISBN 0393971570 confirms Reynolds and 1997.

title: Little Women, Little Men, Jo's Boys (Library of America)
author_or_editor: Louisa May Alcott, ed. Elaine Showalter
reliability_notes: LOA volume listing confirms the 2005 edition with Showalter's introduction and notes. check_first: the LOA volume number (108 vs the series' later numbering) — title, editor, publisher and year are firm.

title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (Mark Twain Library edition)
author_or_editor: Walter Blair and Victor Fischer (eds.), revised edn Victor Fischer and Lin Salamo with Harriet Elinor Smith
reliability_notes: Mark Twain Project/UC Press confirm the MLA text, first published 1985, revised later.

title: The Novels and Tales of Henry James, New York Edition, 24 vols
publisher: Charles Scribner's Sons (New York); simultaneously London: Macmillan
reliability_notes: Bibliographic records confirm 24 vols, Scribner's 1907–09, Macmillan London 1908–09. This is the authoritative revised text James supervised.

title: The Complete Letters of Henry James, 12 vols (ongoing)
author_or_editor: Pierre A. Walker and Greg W. Zacharias (gen. eds.), later series edited with Michael Anesko and Katie Sommer
reliability_notes: Nebraska page one series record confirms the general editors and 2006 start. The task brief's "Harvard/Atlantic edition" of James could not be traced (see UNRESOLVED).

title: The Rise of Silas Lapham
author_or_editor: William Dean Howells, intro. Kermit Vanderbilt
reliability_notes: Penguin record confirms Vanderbilt's introduction and 1983. No full scholarly Howells edition row is used beyond the Ohio State Writings series (checked but not re-dated this pass).

title: A New England Nun and Other Stories
reliability_notes: First-collection imprint confirmed in library catalogs and Freeman scholarship.

title: The Awakening: A Norton Critical Edition, 2nd edn
reliability_notes: Norton record confirms Culley's NCE; a 3rd edn followed in 2018 — cite the edn actually used.

title: The Works of Stephen Crane, 10 vols (University of Virginia Edition)
reliability_notes: Bowers's scholarly texts of Maggie: A Girl of the Streets, The Black Riders, The Red Badge of Courage, George's Mother and Three Stories (1969–1976), confirmed via catalog records for the University of Virginia Publications series.

title: McTeague: A Norton Critical Edition, 2nd edn
reliability_notes: Norton record ISBN 9780393970135 confirms Pizer and 1997; Pizer also edited The Red Badge of Courage NCE (2nd edn, 1976), verified but trimmed — see RESERVE.

title: Jack London: Novels and Social Writings (Library of America, vol. 7)
author_or_editor: Jack London; Library of America edited volume (no named volume editor on the title page)
reliability_notes: LOA confirms vol. 7 (1982) as the London volume gathering the novels and the social writing. check_first: the name of the LOA volume editor — cite the volume itself rather than an editor that is not printed on it.

title: The Columbia Literary History of the United States
reliability_notes: CUP record confirms Elliott as general editor and 1988. check_first: the names of the section/contributing editors as printed; the gen. ed. and publisher/year are firm.

title: American Literature: A Journal of Literary History, Criticism, and Bibliography
author_or_editor: published for the American Literature Section of the MLA
reliability_notes: Duke UP's own series page states "From 1929 to the latest issue" — vol. 1 is 1929, still running.

title: The Cambridge Companion to the Victorian Novel
reliability_notes: Standard Cambridge Companion: first edition 2001, second edition 2012. Essays on the serial, realism, the sensation novel, industrial fiction, and the New Woman novel; used as the critical frame for the British strand, not as a substitute for a primary text.

title: Victorian Studies: A Journal of the Humanities, Arts, and Sciences
reliability_notes: Founded 1957 at Indiana University; the principal interdisciplinary journal of the field. Cited as an ongoing periodical of record for Victorian scholarship, not for any single biographical fact.
